metadata.summary: This guideline examines evidence on how pelvic endometriosis and ovarian endometriomas affect assisted conception outcomes. It addresses management before and during ART, including IUI, IVF/ICSI, oocyte retrieval and embryo transfer. Its recommendations cover medical and surgical approaches, stimulation protocols, infection prevention and other measures intended to improve assisted conception outcomes.

target_population: patients with endometriosis undergoing assisted conception
patients with ovarian endometrioma undergoing ART
therapeutic_areas: complementary therapies, lifestyle measures and supplements

toxicities.event: Reduced ovarian reserve after endometrioma surgery
toxicities.incidence: A cited analysis reported up to 38% reduction in AMH after ovarian cystectomy.
recognition: Poor ovarian response or failure to retrieve oocytes may lead to cycle cancellation.
prevention: Do not routinely operate on ovarian endometriomas before ART solely to improve live birth outcomes.
Consider excision or ablation before ART for symptom control or to make follicles accessible at oocyte retrieval.

toxicities.event: Pituitary oversuppression with prolonged GnRH agonist treatment
prevention: Use caution when considering a longer GnRH agonist protocol in patients with reduced ovarian reserve.

toxicities.event: Pelvic infection or abscess after transvaginal oocyte retrieval
toxicities.incidence: In a retrospective study of 5,958 transvaginal oocyte retrieval procedures, the rate of PID was 0.12%; only one patient out of ten with PID had an ovarian endometrioma. In a separate follow-up study of 214 IVF cycles in patients with persistent endometriomas, no pelvic abscess was reported (0.0, CI 0.0–1.7%).
recognition: Pelvic abscess may present weeks after transvaginal oocyte retrieval.
Patients should report symptoms suggestive of infection after the procedure.

management.severity: Reported pelvic abscess after intentional endometrioma aspiration
management.actions: In a cited case report, the abscess was treated conservatively with antibiotics.

management.severity: Reported pelvic abscess without endometrioma puncture, or ruptured ovarian abscess

prevention: Consider prophylactic antibiotics at oocyte retrieval in patients with endometrioma; the evidence does not support routine use in all patients with endometriosis.
Avoid elective endometrioma aspiration during oocyte retrieval unless follicle access requires it.
If an endometrioma is punctured, consider an extended antibiotic course.

toxicities.incidence: A cited study found a higher recurrence rate after ethanol sclerotherapy than after laparoscopic cystectomy (p=.017); it did not provide a recurrence percentage.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Suppressive hormonal treatment may be considered after endometriosis surgery to limit symptoms and disease recurrence while awaiting ART.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients awaiting ART after endometriosis surgery.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Evidence is insufficient to recommend routine antibiotics at transvaginal oocyte retrieval for all patients with endometriosis, but prophylaxis should be considered when an endometrioma is present.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients with endometrioma undergoing transvaginal oocyte retrieval.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Consider an extended antibiotic course if an ovarian endometrioma is punctured during transvaginal oocyte retrieval.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients whose endometrioma is punctured during transvaginal oocyte retrieval.
prophylaxis.duration: An extended course; the guideline does not specify a duration.

infection_management.pathogen_or_syndrome: Pelvic inflammatory disease following transvaginal oocyte retrieval
infection_management.prevention: Routine prophylactic antibiotics are not supported by sufficient evidence for all patients with endometriosis; consider them when an endometrioma is present. No particular vaginal lavage technique is recommended on the available evidence.
infection_management.management: Patients with endometriosis should be advised to report symptoms suggestive of infection after retrieval.

infection_management.pathogen_or_syndrome: Pelvic abscess following transvaginal oocyte retrieval
infection_management.prevention: Do not electively aspirate an endometrioma unless needed to reach follicles. Consider an extended antibiotic course if puncture occurs.
infection_management.management: A cited abscess case after intentional aspiration was managed with antibiotics alone. Other cited abscess cases, including cases without endometrioma puncture and a ruptured ovarian abscess after aspiration, required surgery.

conditions.name: endometriosis
conditions.description: A chronic inflammatory condition involving tissue resembling endometrium outside the uterus. Associated infertility has multiple proposed contributors, including pelvic adhesions, tubal obstruction, inflammation and hormonal factors. Its effects on assisted reproductive outcomes vary across the studies discussed in the guideline.
conditions.epidemiology: The condition is estimated to affect 10% of women of reproductive age. Up to 50% of women presenting with infertility are estimated to have endometriosis. Estimated monthly fecundability is 2–10% in women with endometriosis, compared with 20% in reproductive-age women without known fertility problems.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Symptoms vary widely, and some patients have none. Infertility and pelvic pain may occur, alongside physical, sexual, psychological and social effects.

subtypes.name: peritoneal
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A pelvic subtype identified by the location of disease.

subtypes.name: deep infiltrating
subtypes.distinguishing_features: May coexist with endometrioma and may involve the bowel.

subtypes.name: ovarian
subtypes.distinguishing_features: May include ovarian endometrioma and be associated with diminished ovarian reserve.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish a diagnosis of endometriosis and assess surgically visible disease.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The studies considered by the guideline included diagnoses made by laparoscopy.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish a diagnosis of endometriosis without surgery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The studies considered by the guideline included diagnoses made by imaging.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess luteal phase function in the evidence discussed by the guideline.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Biopsy findings have been used to demonstrate a luteal phase defect in women with endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess luteal phase function in the evidence discussed by the guideline.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Measurements have been used to demonstrate a luteal phase defect in women with endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify the subgroup examined in a cited study of ovarian stimulation.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Participants in that study were negative for endometrial integrins; the guideline does not establish this as a routine diagnostic criterion.

pathology_markers.expected_result: The cited evidence describes abnormal expression in eutopic endometrial tissue and ectopic endometrial implants.
pathology_markers.clinical_significance: High endometrial aromatase expression is associated with poorer IVF outcomes in the evidence cited by the guideline.

staging.system: revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine (rASRM) classification of endometriosis from 1996
staging.additional_rules: Surgical classification takes account of implant location and size and the severity of adhesions. The guideline does not provide further stage-specific thresholds.

conditions.name: minimal and mild endometriosis
conditions.description: The minimal and mild stages of endometriosis are addressed together when the guideline discusses surgery before assisted reproduction and stimulated intrauterine insemination.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify endometriosis and permit surgical assessment of its extent.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The guideline discusses surgically established minimal and mild disease but does not require laparoscopy for every patient.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose endometriosis without surgery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Imaging-based diagnoses were eligible for the evidence considered by the guideline.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Confirm that the fallopian tubes are patent when considering stimulated IUI.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When assessing infertile patients with minimal and mild endometriosis for IUI.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Confirmed tubal patency is among the conditions specified for considering IUI with gonadotropin stimulation.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess sperm parameters when considering stimulated IUI.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When assessing infertile patients with minimal and mild endometriosis for IUI.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Normal parameters are among the conditions specified for considering IUI with gonadotropin stimulation.

staging.system: revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine (rASRM) classification of endometriosis from 1996
staging.additional_rules: Classification considers implant location and size and the severity of adhesions at surgery.

conditions.name: moderate and severe endometriosis
conditions.description: The guideline addresses these more advanced stages together when considering assisted reproductive outcomes, stimulated IUI, IVF and pituitary downregulation. The systematic reviews it cites associate moderate and severe disease with fewer retrieved oocytes, poorer implantation and lower live birth rates during ART, although other cited studies report differing findings.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose endometriosis and assess disease extent surgically.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The guideline includes studies with laparoscopically established disease.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose endometriosis without surgery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The guideline also includes studies using imaging-based diagnosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish whether the fallopian tubes are patent when assessing IUI as an option.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When considering IUI for infertile patients with moderate and severe endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The guideline discusses the uncertain effectiveness of IUI even when the tubes are patent.

staging.system: revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine (rASRM) classification of endometriosis from 1996
staging.additional_rules: Classification considers implant location and size and the severity of adhesions at surgery.

conditions.name: peritoneal endometriosis
conditions.description: A location-based subtype of endometriosis. The guideline separately discusses patients with minimal peritoneal disease in a study of modified natural cycles.

subtypes.name: minimal peritoneal endometriosis
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Minimal-stage disease located in the peritoneum.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose endometriosis and assess disease at surgery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Laparoscopic diagnoses were included in the guideline's evidence.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose endometriosis without surgery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Imaging-based diagnoses were included in the guideline's evidence.

staging.system: revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine (rASRM) classification of endometriosis from 1996

definitions.description: Minimal endometriosis, the stage specified for the peritoneal subgroup discussed in the modified natural-cycle study.

staging.additional_rules: The classification uses implant location and size and adhesion severity assessed at surgery; the guideline does not assign every case of peritoneal endometriosis to this stage.

conditions.name: deep infiltrating endometriosis
conditions.description: A subtype considered separately in the discussion of surgery before IVF. It often coexists with endometrioma and can involve the bowel. The guideline notes limitations and potential bias in the cited evidence on whether surgery improves IVF outcomes.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose endometriosis and assess disease surgically.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Laparoscopically established endometriosis was included in the evidence reviewed.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose endometriosis without surgery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Imaging-based endometriosis diagnoses were included in the evidence reviewed.

staging.system: revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine (rASRM) classification of endometriosis from 1996
staging.additional_rules: The guideline does not assign a particular rASRM stage to all cases of deep infiltrating endometriosis.

conditions.name: ovarian endometrioma
conditions.description: An ovarian manifestation of endometriosis associated with reduced ovarian reserve and, in some studies, fewer follicles or oocytes retrieved during stimulation. The guideline states that available studies do not establish a precise cyst-size threshold for impaired ovarian response. Excision can further reduce ovarian reserve, particularly with bilateral disease or repeat surgery.
conditions.epidemiology: Ovarian endometriomas are described as occurring in almost 50% of endometriosis cases.
conditions.clinical_presentation: May accompany endometriosis-related symptoms and make follicles less accessible during oocyte retrieval. Histological studies cited by the guideline describe invasion of the ovarian cortex, fibrosis and irregular vascular networks.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose endometriosis without surgery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Imaging-based diagnoses were included in the guideline's evidence.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess ovarian follicles and ovarian reserve.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Women with endometriomas are described as having lower antral follicle counts than women with healthy ovaries or other benign ovarian cysts.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess ovarian reserve.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Levels are described as lower in women with endometriomas than in women with healthy ovaries or other benign ovarian cysts. A reduction of up to 38% after ovarian cystectomy is reported in the cited evidence.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose endometriosis and assess ovarian disease surgically.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Laparoscopic diagnoses were included in the guideline's evidence; the guideline does not present surgery as necessary for every diagnosis.

staging.system: revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine (rASRM) classification of endometriosis from 1996
staging.additional_rules: The guideline does not equate the presence of an ovarian endometrioma with a specific rASRM stage.

therapies_index.name: ART
approved_indications: Assisted conception for patients with endometriosis-associated infertility.

therapies_index.name: IVF
approved_indications: Assisted conception for patients with endometriosis-associated infertility; in moderate and severe endometriosis, it appears to yield better pregnancy rates than IUI when additional risk factors, such as advancing maternal age, are present.

therapies_index.name: IUI with ovarian stimulation using gonadotropins
approved_indications: May be used for infertility with minimal or mild endometriosis when tubal patency and normal seminal fluid parameters are confirmed, particularly after surgical treatment of endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: GnRH agonist therapy
therapies_index.mechanism: Suppresses ovarian activity; prolonged use can excessively suppress the pituitary.
therapies_index.administration: A cited pre-IVF approach used prolonged suppression for 3–6months; a review examined treatment for a minimum 3months. The guideline finds insufficient evidence to recommend pre-ART use to improve live birth rates.
key_toxicities: Prolonged use may cause pituitary oversuppression, potentially leading to poor ovarian response and luteal insufficiency.

therapies_index.name: Decapeptyl
therapies_index.administration: A cited stimulated-IUI trial compared daily Decapeptyl 0.1mg for 2weeks before stimulation with a single dose of 3.75mg Decapeptyl followed 4weeks later by daily Decapeptyl 0.1mg for 2weeks before stimulation.

therapies_index.name: long protocol
therapies_index.administration: In a cited stimulated-IUI trial, daily Decapeptyl 0.1mg was given for 2weeks before the stimulation cycle.

therapies_index.name: ultralong protocol
therapies_index.administration: In a cited stimulated-IUI trial, one dose of 3.75mg Decapeptyl was followed 4weeks later by daily Decapeptyl 0.1mg for 2weeks before ovarian stimulation.

therapies_index.name: GnRH agonist downregulation protocols
therapies_index.mechanism: Suppresses pituitary activity during ovarian stimulation.
approved_indications: May be offered for pituitary downregulation during IVF in patients with endometriosis.
therapies_index.administration: A longer protocol may be considered, particularly after surgery for symptomatic endometriosis, with caution in patients with reduced ovarian reserve.
key_toxicities: Prolonged GnRH agonist use may cause pituitary oversuppression, potentially leading to poor ovarian response and luteal insufficiency.

therapies_index.name: GnRH antagonist downregulation protocols
therapies_index.mechanism: Suppresses pituitary activity during ovarian stimulation.
approved_indications: May be offered for pituitary downregulation during IVF in patients with endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: Elagolix
therapies_index.mechanism: As a GnRH receptor antagonist, it immediately suppresses pituitary gonadotrophins without the initial flare-up described for GnRH agonists.
therapies_index.administration: An ongoing trial examines Elagolix 200mg twice daily for two weeks before IVF; the guideline states that evidence does not currently support GnRH antagonists as pre-ART treatment.

therapies_index.name: hormonal contraceptives
therapies_index.administration: Evidence is insufficient to recommend their use before ART to improve live birth rates.

therapies_index.name: suppressive hormonal therapies
approved_indications: May be considered after endometriosis surgery to prevent associated symptoms and disease recurrence while awaiting ART.
therapies_index.administration: After endometriosis surgery, while awaiting ART.

therapies_index.name: oral progestogens
therapies_index.mechanism: Proposed to prevent a premature LH surge during controlled ovarian stimulation; progestogen downregulation also makes the endometrium unreceptive.
therapies_index.administration: When used for pituitary suppression during stimulation, embryos must be frozen for transfer in a subsequent cycle. Evidence is insufficient to recommend this approach for patients with endometriosis.
key_toxicities: Endometrial unreceptivity during the treatment cycle.

therapies_index.name: medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA)
therapies_index.administration: A cited study administered 4 or 10 mg/day from menstrual cycle day 3 during controlled ovarian stimulation.

therapies_index.name: vaginal progesterone inserts
therapies_index.administration: A cited IVF study examined 100mg vaginal inserts twice or daily, or thrice daily, for luteal support.

therapies_index.name: progesterone vaginal gel
therapies_index.administration: A cited IVF study examined 8% vaginal gel once daily for luteal support.

therapies_index.name: luteal phase support
approved_indications: Patients undergoing IVF should receive the same consideration for luteal phase support whether or not they have endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: aromatase inhibitors
therapies_index.mechanism: Inhibit aromatase; their addition to gonadotropins during ovarian stimulation has been proposed to improve endometrial receptivity and follicular response while reducing gonadotropin requirements.
therapies_index.administration: Evidence is insufficient to recommend their use as pre-ART treatment.

therapies_index.name: Letrozole
therapies_index.mechanism: As an aromatase inhibitor, it has been proposed as an adjunct to gonadotropins during ovarian stimulation.
therapies_index.administration: A cited retrospective study administered daily Letrozole alongside GnRH agonists before IVF. The guideline finds insufficient evidence to recommend letrozole with gonadotropins for ovarian stimulation or its use in frozen embryo transfer cycles.

therapies_index.name: clomiphene citrate
therapies_index.administration: The guideline reports no evidence supporting its addition to gonadotropins for ovarian stimulation in patients with endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: gonadotropins
therapies_index.mechanism: Used to stimulate ovarian follicular development.
approved_indications: Ovarian stimulation during assisted conception, including stimulated IUI for selected patients with minimal or mild endometriosis.
therapies_index.administration: A higher dose may be needed for ovarian stimulation in patients with stage III-IV endometriosis; no particular preparation is preferred.

therapies_index.name: recombinant FSH
therapies_index.administration: The guideline does not prefer this preparation over other gonadotropins for ovarian stimulation in endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: urinary FSH
therapies_index.administration: The guideline does not prefer this preparation over other gonadotropins for ovarian stimulation in endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG)
therapies_index.administration: The guideline does not prefer this preparation over other gonadotropins for ovarian stimulation in endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: controlled ovarian stimulation
approved_indications: Used in assisted-conception cycles for patients with endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: natural cycle IVF
therapies_index.administration: The guideline finds no evidence on which to recommend natural cycles for ART in women with endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: modified natural cycles
therapies_index.administration: The guideline finds no evidence on which to recommend modified natural cycles for ART in women with endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: mild stimulation protocols
therapies_index.administration: The guideline finds no evidence on which to recommend these protocols for ART in women with endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: hCG
therapies_index.administration: A cited study used hCG to trigger final maturation in modified natural cycles; other cited studies examined intrauterine injection before artificial-cycle frozen embryo transfer.

therapies_index.name: natural cycle endometrial preparation
therapies_index.administration: Evidence is insufficient to recommend natural rather than medicated frozen-thawed embryo transfer cycles for patients with endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: artificial cycle regimens
therapies_index.administration: Evidence is insufficient to recommend medicated rather than natural frozen-thawed embryo transfer cycles for patients with endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: hormone replacement and GnRH agonist protocol
therapies_index.administration: Examined in a cited study of frozen embryo transfer cycles in patients with endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: hormone replacement only
therapies_index.administration: Used as the comparison protocol in a cited frozen embryo transfer study.

therapies_index.name: Atosiban
therapies_index.administration: A cited trial administered it 30minutes before frozen embryo transfer; the guideline finds insufficient evidence to support its use in these cycles for endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: freeze-all strategy
therapies_index.mechanism: Defers embryo transfer after ovarian stimulation.
therapies_index.administration: Embryos are frozen for transfer in a later cycle. The guideline states that evidence does not establish superiority over fresh embryo transfer for patients with endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: surgical excision of disease
therapies_index.administration: The guideline calls for further research before routine surgery for minimal to mild endometriosis can be recommended solely to improve subsequent IVF outcomes.

therapies_index.name: surgical cauterization of endometriosis
therapies_index.administration: Performed before GnRH agonist treatment and ART in a cited trial involving minimal and mild endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: ovarian cystectomy
therapies_index.administration: Surgery for ovarian endometrioma should not be routine before ART; excision may be considered for symptom control or to improve follicular access during oocyte retrieval.
key_toxicities: Reduced ovarian reserve; a cited review reported up to 38% reduction in AMH after ovarian cystectomy.
A cited retrospective study found more cycle cancellations from poor ovarian response and/or failed oocyte retrieval after cystectomy.

therapies_index.name: ablation of ovarian endometrioma
approved_indications: May be considered before ART to control endometriosis-associated symptoms or improve access to follicles during oocyte retrieval.
therapies_index.administration: No endometrioma-size threshold for surgery is recommended because evidence is insufficient.

therapies_index.name: sclerotherapy
therapies_index.administration: Examined as a treatment for ovarian endometrioma before ART or at oocyte retrieval.
key_toxicities: A cited study found a higher rate of endometrioma recurrence after sclerotherapy than after laparoscopic cystectomy (p=.017).

therapies_index.name: ethanol sclerotherapy
therapies_index.administration: Performed at the time of oocyte retrieval in a cited study.
key_toxicities: The cited study reported more endometrioma recurrence than after laparoscopic cystectomy (p=.017).

therapies_index.name: transvaginal oocyte retrieval
key_toxicities: Pelvic infection and abscess formation have been reported after retrieval in patients with ovarian endometrioma; the guideline describes the overall risk of pelvic inflammatory disease as low.
monitoring: Counsel women with endometriosis to report symptoms suggestive of infection after retrieval.

therapies_index.name: elective aspiration of an ovarian endometrioma
therapies_index.administration: Not recommended during transvaginal oocyte retrieval unless needed to access follicles. If puncture occurs, consider an extended antibiotic course.
key_toxicities: Pelvic abscess has been reported after endometrioma aspiration during oocyte retrieval.

therapies_index.name: prophylactic antibiotics
approved_indications: May be considered at transvaginal oocyte retrieval for patients with endometrioma; evidence is insufficient to recommend routine use for all patients with endometriosis.
therapies_index.administration: If an endometrioma is punctured during retrieval, consider an extended course. The guideline does not establish a preferred antibiotic, dose or duration.

therapies_index.name: ceftriaxone
therapies_index.administration: A cited retrospective study administered prophylactic intramuscular ceftriaxone at 1g for four days, starting two hours before oocyte retrieval.

therapies_index.name: vaginal lavage
therapies_index.administration: The guideline finds no evidence to recommend a particular lavage technique before transvaginal oocyte retrieval.

therapies_index.name: povidone-iodine
therapies_index.administration: A cited study disinfected the vagina with povidone-iodine before oocyte retrieval, then applied a sterile isotonic saline solution.

therapies_index.name: sterile isotonic saline solution
therapies_index.administration: Used to soak the vagina after povidone-iodine disinfection in a cited oocyte-retrieval study.

therapies_index.name: acupuncture
therapies_index.administration: Discussed for endometriosis-associated pain; its benefit for endometriosis-associated infertility is not supported by evidence in the guideline.

therapies_index.name: yoga
therapies_index.administration: Discussed for endometriosis-associated pain; its benefit for endometriosis-associated infertility is not supported by evidence in the guideline.

therapies_index.name: electrotherapy
therapies_index.administration: Discussed for endometriosis-associated pain; its benefit for endometriosis-associated infertility is not supported by evidence in the guideline.

therapies_index.name: exercise
therapies_index.administration: Discussed for endometriosis-associated pain; its benefit for endometriosis-associated infertility is not supported by evidence in the guideline.

therapies_index.name: antioxidants
therapies_index.administration: The guideline identifies no well-conducted studies establishing benefit for endometriosis-associated infertility.

therapies_index.name: Chinese medicine
therapies_index.administration: The guideline finds no evidence supporting benefit for endometriosis-associated infertility.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients awaiting ART after endometriosis surgery, particularly those with symptoms.
decision_rules: Hormonal suppression may be considered after surgery to limit symptoms and disease recurrence while ART is pending.
Evidence is insufficient to recommend GnRH agonist therapy or hormonal contraceptives before ART for the purpose of improving live birth rates.

recommended_regimens.name: Suppressive hormonal therapies
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider suppression after endometriosis surgery for symptom and recurrence prevention while awaiting ART, rather than as an established means of improving live birth.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A cited RCT involving 400 women with minimal and mild endometriosis found no benefit in embryo quality, implantation or clinical pregnancy after 3months of GnRH agonists following surgical cauterization and before ART.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients considering hormonal pre-treatment before IVF, ICSI or other ART.
decision_rules: Do not present GnRH agonists or hormonal contraceptives as proven to improve live birth when used before ART; evidence is insufficient.
Evidence is insufficient to recommend aromatase inhibitors before ART.
Current evidence does not support GnRH antagonists as pre-treatment; ongoing studies may clarify their role.

not_recommended.name: GnRH agonist therapy or hormonal contraceptives prior to ART to improve live birth rates
not_recommended.reason: Evidence is insufficient to recommend these treatments for this outcome; Good practice point.

not_recommended.name: Aromatase inhibitors as pre-treatment prior to ART
not_recommended.reason: Evidence is insufficient to recommend this approach; Good practice point.

not_recommended.name: GnRH antagonists as pre-treatment prior to ART
not_recommended.reason: There is currently no supporting evidence; further findings from ongoing studies are awaited. Research recommendation.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A Cochrane review of 8 RCTs and 640 participants found uncertain effects of long-term GnRH therapy of minimum 3months on clinical pregnancy, miscarriage and live birth compared with no pre-treatment before IVF or ICSI; the underlying studies were described as very low quality and highly heterogeneous. Prolonged GnRH agonist use may cause pituitary oversuppression, poor ovarian response and luteal insufficiency. A retrospective cohort of 126 women with endometriomas reported improved IVF outcomes with daily Letrozole alongside GnRH agonists, but this does not establish a recommended pre-treatment.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with infertility considering surgery before IVF.
decision_rules: Do not routinely recommend surgery solely to improve IVF outcomes until further research confirms its benefit.

not_recommended.name: Routine surgery for minimal to mild endometriosis prior to IVF
not_recommended.reason: Further research is needed to confirm the apparent benefit before routine surgery can be recommended; Good practice point.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited evidence comparing complete excision with diagnostic laparoscopy alone before IVF/ICSI comes from a single retrospective cohort study (n= 399 versus n=262); it reported better implantation, pregnancy, live birth and cumulative pregnancy outcomes, and a shorter time to first pregnancy after excision.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients considering surgery before IVF, particularly when bowel disease is present.
decision_rules: Do not routinely recommend surgery before IVF solely to improve IVF outcomes without further research.
Individualize decisions with minimal access surgeons in a multidisciplinary team, taking account of the extent of surgery and complication risk.

not_recommended.name: Routine surgery prior to IVF solely to improve IVF outcomes
not_recommended.reason: Further research is required, particularly given the extent of surgery and potential complications in severe disease with bowel involvement; Good practice point.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A meta-analysis of four studies in deep infiltrating endometriosis reported live birth rates 2.2 times (95% CI 1.42–3.46) higher after surgery than without surgery before IVF. Including incomplete-surgery groups also yielded higher pregnancy per patient after surgery (odds ratio [OR] 1.63; 95% CI, 1.16–2.28). No RCTs were included; selection and allocation bias, limited complication data, heterogeneity and a possible imbalance in ovarian endometrioma were identified.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with ovarian endometrioma preparing for ART.
decision_rules: Do not perform endometrioma surgery routinely before ART.
Consider excision or ablation for endometriosis-associated symptom control or to make follicles accessible at oocyte retrieval.
No endometrioma size threshold for pre-ART surgery can be recommended from the available evidence.

alternative_regimens.name: Excision or ablation of ovarian endometrioma
alternative_regimens.summary: Surgery may be considered for symptoms or to improve access to follicles, rather than routinely to improve ART live birth.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Endometriosis-associated symptoms or impaired follicular accessibility during oocyte retrieval; no evidence-based threshold size is specified.

not_recommended.name: Routine surgical management of ovarian endometriomas before ART
not_recommended.reason: Current evidence indicates neither a detrimental live-birth effect from the endometrioma nor a beneficial live-birth effect from its excision, while surgery is likely to diminish ovarian reserve; Strong recommendation.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A cited review found no live-birth improvement after ovarian cystectomy versus no surgery (5 studies, 655 women), or pregnancy improvement (11 studies, 1,512 women). A retrospective comparison found cycle cancellation from poor response and/or failed retrieval of 13.7% versus 0% after cystectomy versus with endometrioma in situ, without a significant live-birth difference (23.7% versus 26.1% with surgery). In a prospective study comparing laparoscopic cystectomy with ethanol sclerotherapy at retrieval, ART outcomes did not differ significantly, but recurrence was higher after sclerotherapy (p=.017). Studies of cyst size and ovarian response were small and of poor overall quality, so a precise size threshold remains uncertain.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients considering complementary therapies, lifestyle interventions or supplements alone or alongside ART.
decision_rules: Further research is necessary before the effectiveness of complementary therapies and lifestyle interventions for infertility, either alone or alongside ART, can be assessed.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The document describes no evidence of an infertility benefit from acupuncture, yoga, electrotherapy, exercise or Chinese medicine, and no well-conducted studies proving a benefit from antioxidants, although some complementary and lifestyle measures have evidence relating to endometriosis-associated pain. This is a Research recommendation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Infertile patients with confirmed tubal patency and normal seminal fluid parameters, especially following surgical management of minimal and mild endometriosis.
decision_rules: IUI with gonadotropin ovarian stimulation may be offered when tubes are patent and semen parameters are normal.
The option is particularly relevant following surgical treatment of minimal and mild disease.

recommended_regimens.name: IUI with ovarian stimulation using gonadotropins
recommended_regimens.summary: An option for eligible infertile patients, especially after surgical management.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A cited RCT reported a livebirth rate 5.6-times higher with stimulated IUI (53 patients with endometriosis) than with expectant management (50 patients with endometriosis), with 95% CI 1.18–17.4.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Low-quality studies suggest gonadotropin-stimulated IUI may improve pregnancy compared with IUI alone (95% CI 1.1–22.5). The document identifies no direct comparison of clomiphene citrate or letrozole against gonadotropins for ovarian stimulation with IUI in endometriosis.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Infertile patients with patent fallopian tubes; advancing maternal age or additional infertility risk factors affect the choice.
decision_rules: The effectiveness of IUI in this population remains unclear.
When additional risk factors are present, particularly advancing maternal age, IVF appears to achieve better pregnancy rates than IUI.

alternative_regimens.name: IVF
alternative_regimens.summary: Compared with stimulated IUI, IVF appears to offer better pregnancy outcomes when additional infertility risks are present.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Additional risk factors such as advancing maternal age; the comparative benefit was especially pronounced in severe disease and women >38 years of age.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: This guidance is a Good practice point. In a retrospective study, pregnancy rates were 47% with IVF (111 patient, 139 cycles), 44% with IVF after failed stimulated IUI (56 patients, 68 cycles), and 11% with stimulated IUI alone (202 patients, 648 cycles). Another retrospective study reported cumulative ongoing pregnancy rates of 40% with stimulated IUI versus 15.6% with an initial unstimulated-IUI approach followed by stimulation if unsuccessful; evidence on IUI in advanced disease was characterized as low quality.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients undergoing IVF with controlled ovarian stimulation, across different stages of endometriosis.
decision_rules: Either GnRH agonist or GnRH antagonist pituitary downregulation may be offered; a difference in clinical pregnancy or live birth has not been demonstrated.
Evidence is insufficient to prefer one of these approaches according to endometriosis stage.
If GnRH agonists are selected, a longer protocol may be considered, particularly after surgery for symptomatic disease, with caution when ovarian reserve is reduced.

recommended_regimens.name: GnRH agonist downregulation protocols
recommended_regimens.summary: An acceptable pituitary downregulation approach for IVF; a longer protocol may be considered in the specified circumstances, subject to ovarian-reserve caution.

recommended_regimens.name: GnRH antagonist downregulation protocols
recommended_regimens.summary: An acceptable alternative approach to pituitary downregulation during IVF, without demonstrated differences in clinical pregnancy and live birth relative to GnRH agonist protocols.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The statement on considering a longer GnRH agonist protocol is a Good practice point. A meta-analysis of 9 RCTs (943 participants) suggested improved clinical pregnancy with an ultra-long GnRH agonist protocol of 3months versus a long protocol (CI 1.11–1.55), without an increase in OHSS; this finding does not establish superiority of GnRH agonists over antagonists. In a retrospective analysis, higher rates per fresh transfer with a GnRH long protocol did not translate into different cumulative live birth rates per cycle.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients undergoing controlled ovarian stimulation for ART, including those with severe endometriosis.
decision_rules: Evidence is insufficient to recommend oral progestogens for pituitary suppression in this population.
A progestogen suppression protocol requires embryos to be frozen and transferred in a later cycle because it makes the endometrium unreceptive.

not_recommended.name: Oral progestogens for pituitary suppression during controlled ovarian stimulation
not_recommended.reason: Evidence is insufficient to recommend their use in endometriosis; Weak recommendation.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: No RCT directly compared oral progestogens against GnRH analogues for this purpose in endometriosis. A retrospective study in advanced disease found no differences in oocyte, embryo or pregnancy outcomes with medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) at 4 or 10 mg/day from menstrual cycle day 3 versus GnRH agonist protocols. In an RCT of 450 women with severe disease, oocyte yield was 9.3±5.7 with MPA, 8.0±4.5 with dydrogesterone and 7.8±5.2 with progesterone; fertilisation and pregnancy outcomes did not differ significantly.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients undergoing ovarian stimulation for ART, particularly those with stage III-IV endometriosis.
decision_rules: Do not favor a particular type of gonadotropin; selection depends on clinician and patient preferences.
Patients with stage III-IV endometriosis may require a higher gonadotropin dose.
Evidence is insufficient to recommend letrozole as an adjunct to gonadotrophins.
There is no evidence supporting addition of clomiphene citrate to gonadotropins in this population.
There is no evidence on which to base recommendations for natural, modified natural or mild-stimulation ART protocols.

recommended_regimens.name: Gonadotropins
recommended_regimens.summary: Choose the gonadotropin preparation according to clinician and patient preferences rather than a demonstrated preference specific to endometriosis; a higher dose may be needed in stage III-IV disease.

not_recommended.name: letrozole as an adjunct to gonadotrophins for ovarian stimulation
not_recommended.reason: Data are insufficient to recommend this adjunct; Good practice point.

not_recommended.name: clomiphene citrate in addition to gonadotropins for ovarian stimulation
not_recommended.reason: There is no evidence supporting this use in patients with endometriosis; Good practice point.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The possibility of requiring a higher gonadotropin dose in stage III-IV disease carries a Strong recommendation. There are no direct studies comparing gonadotropin preparations or doses specifically in endometriosis. Evidence is also lacking to support recommendations for natural, modified natural or mild-stimulation protocols; this is a Good practice point. A cited retrospective study in patients negative for endometrial integrins found higher clinical pregnancy and delivery with letrozole plus gonadotropins than without letrozole, but the guideline nevertheless finds the evidence insufficient for a recommendation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with endometrioma undergoing transvaginal oocyte retrieval.
decision_rules: Routine antibiotic prophylaxis at transvaginal retrieval cannot be recommended on current evidence, but consider it when endometrioma is present.
Do not electively aspirate an endometrioma during retrieval unless follicle access requires it.
If the endometrioma is punctured, consider an extended antibiotic course.
No particular pre-retrieval vaginal lavage technique can be recommended.

alternative_regimens.name: Prophylactic antibiotics
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider prophylaxis at transvaginal oocyte retrieval when an endometrioma is present; no antibiotic regimen is established.

alternative_regimens.name: Elective aspiration of an ovarian endometrioma
alternative_regimens.summary: Aspiration is an exception to the recommendation against elective puncture.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Necessary to access follicles during transvaginal oocyte retrieval.

not_recommended.name: Routine prophylactic antibiotics at transvaginal oocyte retrieval
not_recommended.reason: Evidence is insufficient to recommend routine administration, although prophylaxis should be considered with endometrioma; Good practice point.

not_recommended.name: Elective aspiration of an ovarian endometrioma at oocyte retrieval
not_recommended.reason: Not recommended unless necessary to access follicles; Good practice point.

supportive_care: Consider an extended antibiotic course if an endometrioma is punctured.
Counsel patients to report symptoms suggestive of infection following transvaginal oocyte retrieval.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The retrieval recommendations are Good practice points. No studies evaluated antibiotic type, dose or duration, vaginal lavage protocols, or intentional endometrioma aspiration at retrieval. A retrospective series of 5,958 transvaginal retrievals reported PID in 0.12%. Case reports describe pelvic abscesses after retrieval despite prophylactic antibiotics, including after both punctured and unpunctured endometriomas.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Couples with endometriosis and non-male factor infertility considering the method of fertilisation.
decision_rules: Evidence is insufficient to recommend ICSI instead of standard IVF solely because endometriosis is present without male factor infertility.

not_recommended.name: ICSI over standard IVF solely for endometriosis with non-male factor infertility
not_recommended.reason: Evidence is insufficient to recommend ICSI preferentially; Good practice point.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: In a cited RCT of 786 sibling oocytes, ICSI yielded higher fertilisation than conventional IVF (73.3±23% vs 54.7±31.9%), but implantation, clinical pregnancy, ongoing pregnancy and miscarriage rates did not differ in fresh or frozen cycles.

decision_rules: Evidence is insufficient to recommend natural-cycle rather than medicated-cycle frozen-thawed embryo transfer, or the reverse.
Evidence is insufficient to support letrozole or atosiban during frozen embryo transfer cycles.

not_recommended.name: letrozole in frozen embryo transfer cycles
not_recommended.reason: Evidence is insufficient to support its use in endometriosis; Good practice point.

not_recommended.name: Atosiban in frozen embryo transfer cycles
not_recommended.reason: Evidence is insufficient to support its use in endometriosis; Good practice point.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The document identifies no direct comparison of natural or modified natural cycles against artificial cycles in endometriosis. Retrospective studies reported higher clinical pregnancy with intrauterine hCG before artificial-cycle transfer and higher pregnancy or live birth with GnRH agonist co-treatment in hormone-replacement transfer cycles, but the guideline does not recommend these as preferred approaches. A cited RCT reported higher clinical pregnancy and implantation with Atosiban than control but did not assess live birth.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients considering elective freeze-all and deferred embryo transfer rather than fresh transfer during IVF.
decision_rules: Do not treat elective Freeze all as established to be better than fresh embryo transfer in patients with endometriosis.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline states that there is no evidence that Freeze all is better than fresh embryo transfer; Good practice point. It also reports retrospective studies favoring deferred transfer for some outcomes, including a meta-analysis of six studies of moderate methodologic quality in 3,010 patients that found higher live-birth frequency with frozen than fresh transfer (OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.13–2.08, p= 0.007). No RCT specifically comparing elective freeze-all or segmented IVF with conventional IVF for endometriosis was identified.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients undergoing IVF for whom luteal phase support is being considered.
decision_rules: Do not differentiate luteal phase support according to whether the IVF patient has endometriosis.
supportive_care: Use the same approach to luteal phase support as for IVF patients without endometriosis.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: This is a Good practice point. A low-quality study compared vaginal progesterone inserts 100mg twice or daily (n=94) or thrice daily (n =75) with 8% progesterone vaginal gel once daily (n =100), and found no significant difference in ongoing or biochemical pregnancy rates among groups.

recommendations.statement: Evidence is insufficient to recommend GnRH agonist therapy or hormonal contraceptives before ART for the purpose of improving live birth rates.
recommendations.rationale: Evidence on prolonged GnRH therapy is uncertain, while evidence for other hormonal therapies is limited and of low quality.
recommendations.source_heading: Hormonal therapies as an adjuvant/pre-treatment to IVF > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Suppressive hormonal therapy may be considered after endometriosis surgery to limit symptoms and disease recurrence while ART is awaited.
recommendations.rationale: GnRH agonist therapy after surgery may reduce recurrence and endometrioma formation.
recommendations.source_heading: Hormonal therapies as an adjuvant/pre-treatment to IVF > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Evidence is insufficient to recommend aromatase inhibitors as pretreatment before ART.
recommendations.rationale: Evidence for this approach is limited and of low quality.
recommendations.source_heading: Hormonal therapies as an adjuvant/pre-treatment to IVF > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Supporting evidence for GnRH antagonists as pretreatment before ART is currently unavailable; findings from ongoing studies are awaited.
recommendations.rationale: A trial of Elagolix before IVF is ongoing.
recommendations.source_heading: Hormonal therapies as an adjuvant/pre-treatment to IVF > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: More research is required to verify the benefits of routine surgery for minimal to mild endometriosis before IVF before recommending it.
recommendations.rationale: The comparison with diagnostic laparoscopy rests on a single retrospective cohort study.
recommendations.source_heading: Surgery as an adjuvant/pre-treatment to ART > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Further research is needed before surgery prior to IVF can be recommended solely to improve IVF outcomes in severe endometriosis. Individualise care with minimal access surgeons in a multidisciplinary team.
recommendations.rationale: Treating severe disease can require extensive surgery and carries a risk of complications, particularly with bowel involvement; the available comparative evidence has a high risk of bias.
recommendations.source_heading: Surgery as an adjuvant/pre-treatment to ART > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Investigate complementary therapies and lifestyle interventions for endometriosis-associated infertility before judging their effectiveness, whether used alone or alongside ART.
recommendations.rationale: Evidence of benefit for treating endometriosis-associated infertility is lacking.
recommendations.source_heading: Complementary therapies, lifestyle measures and supplements > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: IUI with ovarian stimulation using gonadotropins may be offered to infertile patients with minimal to mild endometriosis, confirmed tubal patency and normal seminal fluid parameters, particularly after surgical treatment of minimal to mild disease.
recommendations.context: IUI in minimal to mild endometriosis
recommendations.rationale: Limited evidence suggests that stimulated IUI may improve pregnancy outcomes in this population.
recommendations.source_heading: Effects of endometriosis on intrauterine insemination > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: The effectiveness of IUI for infertile patients with moderate to severe endometriosis and patent fallopian tubes is uncertain. When additional risk factors such as advancing maternal age are present, IVF appears to yield better pregnancy rates.
recommendations.context: IUI in moderate to severe endometriosis
recommendations.rationale: Evidence in advanced disease is of low quality, while comparative data suggest a pregnancy-rate advantage with IVF.
recommendations.source_heading: Effects of endometriosis on intrauterine insemination > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Do not routinely operate on ovarian endometriomas before ART.
recommendations.rationale: Current evidence indicates neither a negative effect of an endometrioma nor a positive effect of its excision on live birth rates, whereas surgery is likely to diminish ovarian reserve.
recommendations.source_heading: Effects of endometrioma surgery on ART outcomes > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Excision or ablation of an ovarian endometrioma before ART may be considered to control endometriosis-associated symptoms or improve access to follicles at oocyte retrieval. Evidence is insufficient to specify a cyst-size threshold for surgery.
recommendations.rationale: Available studies do not establish a precise endometrioma-size threshold that adversely affects ovarian response.
recommendations.source_heading: Effects of endometrioma surgery on ART outcomes > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Either GnRH agonist or GnRH antagonist downregulation may be offered during IVF for patients with endometriosis; clinical pregnancy and live birth rates have not been shown to differ.
recommendations.rationale: Comparisons have not demonstrated a difference in clinical pregnancy and live birth rates.
recommendations.source_heading: Pituitary downregulation protocols during ovarian stimulation > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Data are insufficient to favour GnRH agonist over GnRH antagonist protocols, or the reverse, for particular stages of endometriosis.
recommendations.rationale: Stage-specific comparative findings do not establish a preferred protocol.
recommendations.source_heading: Pituitary downregulation protocols during ovarian stimulation > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: If GnRH agonists are chosen, a longer protocol may be considered, particularly after surgery for symptomatic endometriosis; use caution when ovarian reserve is reduced.
recommendations.rationale: Studies suggest a possible clinical pregnancy benefit with longer protocols, but prolonged suppression raises concern about poor ovarian response.
recommendations.source_heading: Pituitary downregulation protocols during ovarian stimulation > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Evidence is insufficient to recommend oral progestogens for pituitary suppression during controlled ovarian stimulation in patients with endometriosis.
recommendations.rationale: No RCTs directly compare oral progestogens with GnRH analogues for this purpose in patients with endometriosis.
recommendations.source_heading: Pituitary downregulation protocols during ovarian stimulation > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Do not prefer one gonadotropin preparation over another for ovarian stimulation in patients with endometriosis; selection should reflect clinician and patient preferences.
recommendations.rationale: Preparations and their dose effects have not been directly compared in this population.
recommendations.source_heading: Ovarian stimulation protocols Gonadotropins > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Ovarian stimulation in patients with stage III-IV endometriosis may require a higher gonadotropin dose.
recommendations.context: Ovarian stimulation in stage III-IV endometriosis
recommendations.rationale: Patients with ovarian endometriosis may respond less well to gonadotropins and require higher doses.
recommendations.source_heading: Ovarian stimulation protocols Gonadotropins > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Data are insufficient to recommend adding letrozole to gonadotrophins for ovarian stimulation in women with endometriosis.
recommendations.rationale: Available studies do not provide enough evidence to support this combination.
recommendations.source_heading: Ovarian stimulation protocols Gonadotropins > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: No evidence is available for adding clomiphene citrate to gonadotropins for ovarian stimulation in patients with endometriosis.
recommendations.rationale: No RCTs have assessed the benefit of this addition in patients with endometriosis.
recommendations.source_heading: Ovarian stimulation protocols Gonadotropins > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Evidence does not permit recommendations on natural cycles, modified natural cycles or mild stimulation protocols for women with endometriosis undergoing ART.
recommendations.rationale: Conventional IVF has not been compared with natural cycle IVF in this population.
recommendations.source_heading: Ovarian stimulation protocols Gonadotropins > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Evidence is insufficient to recommend routine prophylactic antibiotics at transvaginal oocyte retrieval for patients with endometriosis, but prophylaxis should be considered when an endometrioma is present.
recommendations.rationale: Pelvic infection appears uncommon, and antibiotic prophylaxis has not been adequately evaluated.
recommendations.source_heading: Prophylactic antibiotics at the time of oocyte retrieval > Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Evidence does not support recommending a particular vaginal lavage technique before transvaginal oocyte retrieval.
recommendations.rationale: Different vaginal lavage protocols have not been evaluated in studies.

recommendations.statement: Do not electively aspirate an ovarian endometrioma during transvaginal oocyte retrieval unless doing so is necessary to access follicles. If puncture occurs, consider a longer antibiotic course.
recommendations.rationale: Pelvic abscesses have been reported after retrieval, while evidence on intentional endometrioma aspiration and antibiotic regimens is lacking.
